author: rdc-rfc1-author-a (Claude Haiku 5.5)
rationale: The counter's only asynchronous reset comes from the black-box power-on generator por_gen, so its release timing, clock alignment and glitch freedom cannot be decided.

author_reading.rationale: The reset comes from an opaque generator whose module is not supplied, so its release behaviour and clock domain cannot be decided.

labels.rationale: The async reset comes from por_gen, an opaque library cell with no body. Whether its output is synchronised, glitch-free or released safely cannot be decided. ext_pin is an unconstrained input that feeds only this opaque cell, so no RDC-002 is raised.
labels.detection_gap: ext_pin feeds the opaque reset generator with no set_input_delay. RDC-002 covers only combinational or gated reset roots, so the unconstrained input into a black box is not reported.

labels.rationale: The missing power-on generator is the only intended driver of the counter reset. The interface gives no assertion or release contract.
labels.suspected_flaw: The cell is defined as an empty module without a black-box attribute. Its output is undriven in the literal RTL.

settlement.rationale: Both readers are right: unknown, inventory class. The settler added (* black_box *) to por_gen on line 3, fixing B's flaw that the empty module made the reset literally undriven. CST-005 now reports the black box, and RDC-001 and RDC-003 report a black-box reset root. RDC-013 is a run-level obligation and is not counted.
